clue.text: Rubbery chop fed through lips of cabby

indicators.note: a filling fed through something sits within it, so the chopping word goes inside
the lips of a word are its outer edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: to chop wood is to hew it

explanation.surface: A tough cut of meat is pushed between a taxi driver's lips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lips of' takes the first and last letters of cabby, C and Y, and 'fed through' puts HEW between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is chewy has a rubbery, resilient texture that needs much chewing.

clue.text: Cuttings from this item witnessed by journalist?

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, usually a jobbing one
saw means witnessed

explanation.surface: Press cuttings from an event witnessed by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuttings' suggests press clippings, but here it is what a saw cuts off.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, the tool producing those cuttings.

clue.text: Untidy drawer with big tool on top of enormous spanner

indicators.note: untidy means jumbled, so the letters are mixed up
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A messy drawer has a big tool lying on a huge spanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untidy' yields WATERLOOBRIDG; in a down clue 'on top of' places it above the first letter of enormous. A spanner is anything that spans, here a bridge over the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo Bridge spans the River Thames in London, so it is a spanner in the bridging sense.

definitions.meaning: to ... a play or a performance is to criticise it harshly
a ... is a running account or tab, as in putting drinks on the ...

explanation.surface: Criticise bill
explanation.definitionFit: Slate as a verb is to attack in print; as a noun it is a tally of what is owed, a tab.

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships
something ... weighs less and so floats more easily

explanation.surface: A boat that is less likely to sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge for unloading ships; weighing less makes a thing lighter and more buoyant.

clue.text: An arm and a leg work on puppet covered in sticky substance

indicators.note: being covered in something means it surrounds you, so the sticky word goes round

parts.note: tar is a black sticky substance
op is short for opus, a work
a doll is a toy figure, like a puppet

explanation.surface: A limb and a leg on a puppet get covered in goo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An arm and a leg' is an idiom for a very high price, not body parts; 'covered in' signals the surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying top dollar means paying the highest price, which is what costing an arm and a leg means.

clue.text: Piece of eight in your pocket

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of eight, the old Spanish coin, sitting in your pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Pocket as an adjective means very small, as in a pocket edition, so it means tiny.

definitions.meaning: an idiom for scattered and disordered
aisles run throughout a shop, literally all over it

explanation.surface: Higgledy-piggledy location of aisles?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a mess; read literally, aisles are found right through a store.

clue.text: Good filling a hole up in puzzle

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so the good letter sits within the other letters
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a mine is a hole dug in the ground

explanation.surface: Good stuff fills up a hole, which is puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns A MINE into ENIMA, and 'filling' puts G inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something puzzling.

clue.text: Cold, as night unfortunately closes in — bitter

indicators.note: the rearranged letters close in around the cold letter, holding it inside
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A chilly evening closes in, leaving everyone feeling bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunately' yields SATHING, and 'closes in' wraps that round the cold letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathing criticism is harsh and caustic, the same sense as bitter remarks.

indicators.note: accessing means getting inside, so the shortened road goes into the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A rural road nearly reaches a country school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the road word, and 'accessing' sends it inside the school, a group of whales rather than pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Poland is a nation of central Europe, so it is a country.

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
a tray serves food and drinks to the table

explanation.surface: Someone is wrong, just as a waiter can be.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to go wrong, straying from the right path.

parts.note: tho is an informal spelling of though, which can mean but
a rough estimate is an imprecise one

explanation.surface: Careful in method, yet inexact in the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough work is careful and complete in every detail, which is to be meticulous.

parts.note: a frog moves by hopping, so is an example of a hopper

explanation.surface: A fairy tale featuring a frog, such as the frog prince.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy story' is a colloquial term for a lie, not a tale of fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is a huge lie, and a fairy story is a fanciful untruth.

clue.text: Star name prodding female and male animals

indicators.note: prodding pokes in between, so the name word goes inside the animals

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a ram is a male sheep
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A famous name pokes at female and male animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prodding' pokes the name in between the two animals; the female is a swan, not a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star figure, drawn with one continuous line.

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way is a method or system of doing things

explanation.surface: A general devises a system to allow for some freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to move or slack, as is play in a rope or mechanism.

clue.text: Article and edict from Greek city

parts.note: the is the definite article
a ban is an official prohibition, an edict

explanation.surface: A decree and its legal text issued from an ancient Greek city.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a powerful city of ancient Greece; a Theban is a native of it.

definitions.meaning: a ... welcome is warm and friendly
an old salt is a sailor, and so is a ..., as in me hearties

explanation.surface: Warm salt
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty means cordial and warm; hearty is also an old term for a sailor, as is salt.

clue.text: Something flat in the sky, pie thrown about in Texas, say?

indicators.note: in places the turned-round pie inside the letters for a southern American state

parts.note: Texas is a state in the south of the US, giving S for south and US

indicators.note: thrown about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tart is a pie, often open

explanation.surface: Someone flings a pie in Texas, and something flat is overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown about' gives TRAT; 'in' places it within the letters for Texas, a southern American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a cloud forming a flat, uniform grey layer across the sky.

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the shortened word
briefly means cut short, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a kennel is a shelter for a dog
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dog — could it be one in a kennel for a short stay?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims SHELTER to SHELTE, and 'in' places I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltie is a Shetland sheepdog, a small breed of dog.

clue.text: Princesses welcoming me being upset in class

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
welcoming means taking in, so the princesses hold the other word

parts.note: ranis are Indian princesses or queens

explanation.surface: Royal ladies are upset when they let me into their lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcoming' gives RANIMES, and 'being upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a teaching session for a small group, a class.

clue.text: Award garlands in a witty conversation

indicators.note: to garland is to encircle, so the award word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a badge is awarded, for instance to a scout

explanation.surface: An award is presented with flowers amid clever chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, teasing banter, which is witty conversation.

indicators.note: brewing mixes things up, so the letters of teas are rearranged

parts.note: well and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Hot tea, well brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' yields STEA; 'well' is an exclamation, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes something humid and hot, giving off steam.

indicators.note: sending things skyward in a down clue lifts the word to read from the bottom up
skyward in a down clue means upwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: auks are other seabirds, short-winged divers

explanation.surface: A bird makes others take flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Others' means other birds, AUKS, which 'sending skyward' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a large predatory seabird that robs other birds of their catch.

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, which is taken away

parts.note: to stagger someone is to shock them

explanation.surface: An old soldier is in shock and has lost his nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' removes the middle G of STAGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is someone long experienced in an activity, a veteran.

indicators.note: a defender surrounds and protects, so the shortened word goes round the punch word
cut means a word is docked of its last letter

parts.note: a tough is a rough brute, a thug
to chin someone is to punch them on the chin

explanation.surface: A thug, wounded, holds off a blow in an emotional scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' gives TOUG, which 'defending' wraps round the punch; to chin someone is slang for hitting them on the jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something touching moves the feelings, so it is emotional.

definitions.note: read here as glow-er, a thing that glows, a noun

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a member of a club is an associate of it

explanation.surface: A colleague, losing his head, scowls at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a scowl but is read as glow-er, something that glows.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a smouldering piece of coal that still glows after a fire.

definitions.meaning: Muriel ... was a Scottish novelist, author of The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie

explanation.surface: Flash Scottish author
explanation.definitionFit: A spark is a tiny flash of fire; Muriel Spark is a celebrated Scottish writer.
